one_paragraph_summary: Delivered November 27, 2014 at the 25th Death Anniversary commemoration of CJ Claudio Teehankee, this address by CJP delivers three messages. First, thanks to the Claudio Teehankee Foundation for conferring on him the Rule of Law Award on April 13, 2013 and inviting him to join its Board of Trustees. He greets CJ Hilario Davide Jr. (Foundation chairman and CJP's predecessor, whose Action Program for Judicial Reform 'became the exemplar or model of the World Bank in judicial reforms,' a program CJP continued), Justice Arturo Brion (Ateneo valedictorian and bar topnotcher like Teehankee), and Ambassador Manuel Dondi Teehankee ('worthy son of the worthy father'). Second, tribute to Teehankee: summa cum laude in both preparatory law and LLB from 'the best university in the Philippines'; his mentor Salonga warned whenever facing Teehankee: 'You better prepare our trial brief very well because we are going to be on the opposite side of one of the best lawyers in town.' Teehankee pioneered the libertarian philosophy, 'nearly died for it,' was bypassed twice for CJ under Marcos ('it is easy to be brave during peace time like now, but during the Martial Law years, there were many gifted public officials but few had the courage to stand up for their convictions'), and was finally appointed 16th CJ by Cory Aquino in 1986. Spotting Oscar Lopez at the back of the auditorium, CJP extends the same tribute to the Lopez Group, which 'stood up against President Marcos... undaunted and stood up for dignity, honor and country.' Third, the FLP-Teehankee Foundation kindredship: Teehankee's libertarian philosophy is embedded in the Constitution; FLP extends it to economic freedom -- 'it is not just the political liberty of our people that we must serve, protect and promote. We must also serve, protect and promote economic freedom.' Businessmen who benefit most from free enterprise 'have the obligation to share their benefits with their workers and their fellow Filipinos, so we can all conquer poverty and ultimately share prosperity.'
